items.requirement: A requested check fails when its build output is missing.
The check consumes one explicit typed build artifact and does not guess a directory.
The input can represent one binary, one archive, one application package, or one set of web assets.
The provider verifies the input size, content digest, media type, and local artifact URL.
The result reports total output size.
The result reports the output file count.
The result reports the largest files in descending size order.
Measurements use exact content bytes instead of file-system allocation blocks and rounded kilobytes.
A compressed archive reports its stored compressed bytes and expanded content bytes.
A maximum total size can fail the check.
A maximum file count can fail the check.
A limit breach cannot pass a blocking check.
A named pattern can limit the sum of matching file bytes.
A required pattern fails when no file matches it.
A stored baseline can limit absolute growth in bytes.
A stored baseline can limit percentage growth.
A blocking check requires at least one explicit limit.
An advisory check can report measurements without a limit.
Each completed measurement produces a typed immutable baseline artifact.
A growth check verifies the baseline size, digest, media type, and schema.
The result records a pass or fail with structured findings.
The result stores exact metrics, matching-file facts, growth facts, and largest-file facts.
Bounded logs and the baseline artifact remain stored evidence.
Archive paths reject absolute paths, parent traversal, empty segments, and duplicate entries.
Archive symbolic links, hard links, devices, and unsupported extension records are rejected.
Input bytes, expanded bytes, file count, path length, patterns, evidence, time, and memory are bounded.
The provider does not extract archive content or access a network service.
Timeout and cancellation cannot produce a passing blocking result.
Retries use independent attempts and preserve all attempt results.
The check runs after artifact creation and before live tests.
The check does not deploy, expose, open a browser, or contact an agent.
A symbolic link must not escape the selected output and add external file bytes.
A partial directory scan must not pass an enforced budget as complete evidence.
The replacement cannot control the gate during implementation or parity.
The old bundle suite remains the sole authority until cutover.
